text:
jana: Observed flaky behaviour in the demo chat: after ~20-40s of a long generation the client stops emitting any onmessage callbacks even though network shows SSE frames still being delivered. Happens in Chrome/Firefox, ~25% runs.

oliver: Any console errors? Network tab shows 200 and frames?

jana: Console silent. Network shows continuous response body growth. I captured raw bytes: when reconnect happens (token rotate) we sometimes get a fragment split inside JSON (e.g. 'data: {"choices": ["par' then on reconnect 'tial"]}

'). The client parser treats the first fragment as a complete event and the second as a new unrelated event, causing JSON.parse errors or silent drops.

sam: This is similar to the parsing tolerance issue we saw earlier, but different in that the partial fragment is not followed by an empty line on the same connection. Browser EventSource implementations can coalesce or flush differently on abort.

jana: Repro steps I used (headless): 1) start demo with short-lived demo token (TTL 30s) 2) send prompt that streams ~60 tokens over 30s 3) rotate token on session refresh 4) observe client output stops. I attached a small tcpdump and the headless run trace in the sampleapp branch `demo-sse-resume` and a short script that reproduces the split.

oliver: Quick triage: is the last-event-id header correctly sent on reconnect? If last-event-id points to a resume checkpoint, we must ensure the server emits a full checkpoint event boundary. If server resends a fragment that completes the JSON, client parser must reassemble.

jana: last-event-id is present, but server replays only the tail fragment; the replayed fragment doesn't include the leading 'data:' line separator in some cases. Looks like our reconnect code strips the first CRLF during handshake.

sam: Actionable fixes: 1) browser SDK: make SSE parser tolerant to fragment reassembly across reconnects. Keep a small rolling buffer of the last incomplete 'data:' payload and attempt to prepend it when a reconnect with last-event-id occurs. 2) Server: when honoring resume, ensure replayed payloads start at event boundary (prepend newline if needed). 3) Demo config: extend token TTL for onboarding flows as a short-term mitigation.

oliver: I'll open a server-side change to guarantee event-boundary preservation on resume. Jana, can you add a failing unit for the client that reproduces the split frames? We should simulate: frameA='data: {"text":"par' then reconnect+frameB='tial"}

' and assert the final emitted message is the merged JSON.

jana: Yep, adding that test and a Puppeteer e2e that runs 200 iterations to validate stability. Also adding a lightweight telemetry event `sse.fragment_reassembly_failure` to ping us if this happens in hosted.

sam: For the SDK patch, let's gate the reassembly behind a feature flag (streaming.reassembly=true) so we can roll it out. Also add an opt-out strict mode for customers who rely on stricter event boundaries. We'll mirror the same behavior in the Node SDK for parity.

oliver: PRs: server #2031 (ensure resume boundaries), browser-sdk #948 (reassembly + flag + tests), sampleapp #312 (extend demo token TTL + repro harness). ci-bot: queued.

ci-bot: Build started for PR #948, #2031, #312.

jana: Short-term workaround for demo env: bump demo token TTL to 5 minutes and flip streaming.reassembly=true in the sampleapp config. That should unblock onboarding while we land tests.

sam: After landing, we'll run stress runs: puppeteer 500 loops and a synthetic load test that rotates tokens frequently. If telemetry spikes, we'll revert the flag.

jana: Thanks team 60a If anyone sees odd hangs in staging, ping me with trace and tcpdump.

oliver: Nice catch. We'll follow up with a postmortem note in the repo once we verify stability.
